rv.q: But you never fully feel like you watching human beings in crisis.
THE ALLY is an intentionally uncomfortable yet essential work for contemporary audiences.
But as an expression of the struggle we experience societally, through the vehicle of the conflicted Asaf—that weakness doesn’t hamper the impact and value of “The Ally.”
Wechsler's cast, particularly Shappell and Ghaeini, are compelling to watch even when the discourse feels like it's veering into occasional repetition.
THE ALLY will impress. It will make theatergoers think. And, hopefully, it will inspire audiences to listen to other people's voices.
Perhaps it’s just an unpleasant play.
This is a story that deals with what one truly believes is right versus what one might "think" is right or for that matter, even "feel" right!

If you’re interested in the events of the day and have the capacity to take in a lot of information while considering opposing ideas you will find this a thought-provoking presentation in an entertaining package.

cn.t: Moses' Pulitzer-nominated drama provokes thought with urgent questions about Israel-Palestine, but critics split on whether it's compelling theater or just debate. Strong performances can't fully overcome a talky, argument-heavy structure.
